overallNotes: Monica Renee Halverson (personal_11) is a richly drawn persona spanning nearly 4 years (Jan 2025 - Aug 2028) of a 40-year-old senior housing code inspector turned frontline supervisor in Milwaukee's Department of Neighborhood Services. Her arc traces the transformation of a personal commitment to safer north-side rental stock into a formal two-corridor enforcement model with documented safer-housing outcomes. The narrative sustains strong continuity across work, health, family, and personal life through 30 slices. Key patterns: (1) Professional growth from newly promoted supervisor to corridor-program architect defending concentrated enforcement at leadership level — setbacks (political interference after exposing prominent owners, budget threats) are met with tighter documentation and process redesign rather than retreat. (2) Asthma is managed with increasing precision — an urgent care scare in spring 2025 leads to stricter inhaler routines, mask protocols, and exposure planning that holds across subsequent years. (3) Co-parenting with Travis evolves from tense ad-hoc texting to shared spreadsheets and Sunday check-ins; Leah's transition from middle school to high school choices becomes a recurrent structural theme. (4) Relationship arc: cautious dating of Colin Mercer ends in winter 2026 over schedule mismatch and emotional fatigue; after a long reset she begins cautiously dating Naomi Sato (archivist) in spring 2028 with greater clarity about what fits her life. (5) Key supporting figures are well-defined: Andre Pruitt (veteran inspector/pattern-reader), Denise Wroblewski (retiring mentor), Shawna Brooks (close friend/social worker), and Colin Mercer / Naomi Sato (romantic partners). (6) Personal interests layer naturally — Milwaukee neighborhood history reading becomes a deliberate counterweight to work stress; Brewers games with Leah create car-ride connection rituals; Sunday night courtroom movies become a reset habit; public radio evening programs lower the after-work emotional temperature. CRITICAL ISSUE with current metadata: ALL 30 slices have emotional_tone: 'neutral' which is clearly incorrect — emotional tones vary significantly (positive for personal discoveries and wins, negative for political setbacks, mixed for ambiguous transitions). Tags are identical generic categories (work/family/health/finance/housing/education/leisure/goals) applied indiscriminately with no specificity. Nearly ALL summary fields are literal quote fragments from the user's first turn rather than genuine summaries of conversation content. Many focus fields are truncated mid-word. There is no open_loops field on any slice. Decisions fields are generally well-maintained though occasionally truncated.
